summary: encrypt-string-safe fetches and executes remote JavaScript from an obfuscated CDN URL on library use
details: index.js is heavily obfuscated with an obfuscator.io-style rotated custom-base64 string array. The exported encrypt/decrypt/admin APIs route through an ensureCore() helper that fetches text from a hardcoded CDN URL hidden as string-array index 0x85 and passes the response body to `new Function('CryptoJS', 'return ' + code +...)`, then invokes the constructed function to obtain the real implementation. There is no hash or signature check on the fetched code — only a weak `__esaCore` marker substring and a regex. Any consumer that imports and calls this library grants the CDN operator arbitrary JavaScript execution inside the installer's Node.js process. The obfuscation of the URL, the `Function` template, and the fetch options exists to conceal this remote-code-loading channel; a crypto-string helper has no legitimate reason to source its implementation from a remote endpoint at runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
